beats.text: Six lines from literature that still stop readers in their tracks.
"It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done." — A Tale of Two Cities.
"So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past." — The Great Gatsby.
"Whatever our souls are made of, his and mine are the same." — Wuthering Heights.
"We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars." — Oscar Wilde.
"To be, or not to be, that is the question." — Hamlet, still the loudest four centuries on.
Great writers die. Their best sentences refuse to. Which one stays with you?
